name: Yurakucho
tagline: Tokyo in 2 minutes and Otemachi in 2 minutes. Served by 6 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥160,000 to ¥170,000.
summary: The station is in Chiyoda City, where JR East, Tokyo Metro and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 6 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 2 minutes to Otemachi, 20 minutes to Shinjuku, 19 minutes to Shibuya and 12 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. The station stands 2.7 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 1.8 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 2.7 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 1.9 m to 3.7 m, a difference of 1.8 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 7 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 4 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is about average for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 10 clinics and 8 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 浩邦会日比谷病院, about 13 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 十仁病院, about 15 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 6 lines serve the station. JR Yamanote Line and JR Keihin-Tohoku Line run through it. Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line also call here. Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line are available too. Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line stop here as well. Toei Mita Line stop here as well. The lines are split between operators (JR East runs 2 lines, Tokyo Metro runs 3 lines and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line runs at 163% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 三ノ輪→入谷, which this station is not on. JR Keihin-Tohoku Line runs at 159%. Its busiest stretch is 大井町→品川, which this station is likewise not on. Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line runs at 153%. Its busiest stretch is 東池袋→護国寺, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥160,000 to ¥170,000 and 1LDK ¥210,000 to ¥220,000. 2LDK ¥360,000 to ¥370,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is among the lowest in the 23 wards. 6 lines and a wide choice of connections and plenty of places to eat out pushes the figure up. On the other side, little daily shopping within walking distance holds it down.

neighbours.lead: For how close the centre is, Ginza; for rail connections, Yurakucho.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Yurakucho. Ginza has 4 lines, so Yurakucho is the better connected. To Shinjuku, for instance, Ginza is 4 minutes quicker. Rents, flood projections and the rest differ little.

neighbours.lead: Yurakucho is ahead on rail connections and how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Yurakucho. Nijubashimae has only the Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line, so Yurakucho is the better connected. To Toranomon, for instance, Nijubashimae takes 7 minutes longer. Rents, flood projections and the rest differ little.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who want another route when a line stops
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
People who want to hold the rent down
noiseSources: 大名小路 (2 lanes each way) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road
晴海通り (3 lanes each way) runs just outside the station. Traffic on it never stops

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 1 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 7 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 6 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
